projects.summary: Reads a company's invoice export and reports, invoice by invoice, which mandatory fields are missing or malformed for a UAE e-invoice.
overview: The UAE is introducing mandatory e-invoicing in the PINT-AE format. Most businesses do not know whether the invoices their accounting system produces today carry the fields it requires. This tool gives a first answer from an export.

It reads a CSV or Excel export, checks every invoice against the Ministry of Finance mandatory-fields document, and writes a readiness report and a findings file: which invoices pass those checks, which fail them, and what to fix first. Passing does not mean an invoice is fully PINT-AE compliant; it means the mandatory fields are there.

Each rule is tagged by how certain it is: stated in the official document, plain arithmetic, or an assumption that still needs confirming against the specification. The report never presents a guess as a requirement.
projects.roleNote: Design and build of the validator and its report.
projects.statusNote: The validator is built and tested against a fictional sample dataset. It checks the Ministry of Finance mandatory fields. The full PINT-AE schema rules are not checked yet.

projects.summary: A multi-tenant service that takes a restaurant's menu as PDFs or photos and turns it into structured menu data a point-of-sale system can import.
projects.category: Menu digitisation SaaS for restaurants and POS systems
overview: Restaurants keep their menus as PDFs and photos. Point-of-sale and delivery systems need them as structured data: items, prices and options. Retyping is slow and goes wrong.

The service is a modular monolith: a Next.js web app, a FastAPI service, PostgreSQL as both the database and the task queue, and separate worker processes for document handling. Every record is isolated per organisation with row-level security.

Today it gets as far as every page of every uploaded file rendered to an image, with its text extracted and positioned. Progress, per-page results, failures, retry and cancel are all visible in the app.
projects.statusNote: Accounts, organisations, roles, restaurants and menu import are built: uploaded files are rendered page by page and their text is extracted, with OCR for scans. Turning that text into products and prices, the menu editor and the exports are not built yet.

It shows the validity of the documents and notify you

points: I designed and built the whole product: the database, the backend, the web portal and the mobile app. I started by writing the product spec and laying out every screen on a design canvas. After that I built it in small slices, around 35 so far, each one tested before the next began.
projects.summary: A back office for independent UAE restaurants that tracks salaries, post-dated cheques and document renewals so the owner never misses one, and works alongside the POS they already use.
projects.category: Back-office system for companies or businesses in the UAE
overview:
Daftar is a back office SOFTWARE for independent businesses or SME in the UAE with one to more branch. Most of these owners run payroll, cheques and licence renewals out of Excel, WhatsApp and paper chequebooks and more. Daftar puts that work in one place without replacing the restaurant’s POS.
The owner and office team use a web portal. It covers company documents with expiry tracking, a calendar of post-dated cheques, employee records, rosters and attendance, leave, and payroll. Payroll produces WPS salary files and payslips but never moves money itself. The portal also handles expenses, supplier bills, daily sales, profit and loss by outlet, VAT summaries, bank statement matching, and exports to Tally Prime.

points: Designed the schema and wrote the migrations, including the Row Level Security policies and the isolation tests that check them.
Built the tenant, owner, guardian and admin areas end to end.
Built the visit-booking workflow as a role-aware state machine with an audit trail.
Integrated Razorpay payments with a webhook, and a permanent, printable receipt system.
Built the owner management modules: rooms and beds, tenancies, rent engine, utility splitting, mess manager and late-fee automation.
pg-india.summary: A marketplace for paying-guest housing joined to the software owners use to run the building, so a listing reflects real beds instead of a stale advert.
overview: Tenants search and compare listings, request a visit, book, pay, and then live in a dashboard with rent, meals, complaints, agreements and notices. A guardian can follow along through a tokenised link.
Owners register, pass KYC, and then run their property: capacity by room and bed, who is in which bed, what rent is due, how the electricity bill splits, how many plates the kitchen needs tonight.
Admins verify owners and tenants, moderate listings, mediate visits and handle disputes, payments and support.
pg-india.roleNote: Every commit in the web application's repository is mine: product decisions, schema, security rules, interface and integration work.
pg-india.statusNote: Not publicly launched. There are no user, listing or transaction numbers to report, so none are shown.

ventureworld.summary: A marketplace where businesses for sale or seeking investment are listed, reviewed and matched with investors, with AI assistance for writing the listing.

Investors browse opportunities by industry, complete a profile questionnaire and receive recommended listings.
